For the most reliable protection, open VPN settings, tap the gear next to AdVault and enable “Always-on VPN”. Leave “Block connections without VPN” off unless you understand the effect.
AdVault is exempt from battery optimisation.
Android may stop AdVault in the background. Set AdVault to “Unrestricted” / “Not optimised”.
AdVault\'s VPN runs as a foreground service. If protection stops by itself, exempt AdVault from battery optimisation and enable Always-on VPN.
One UI can put apps to sleep. Open Settings › Battery › Background usage limits and add AdVault to “Never sleeping apps”. Also set Apps › AdVault › Battery to “Unrestricted”.

A personal, on-device DNS ad blocker for Android. Built for sideloaded personal use.
Everything runs locally. The VPN is on-device only; there is no AdVault server and your traffic never leaves through us.
No tracking, analytics or advertising SDKs inside AdVault.
No HTTPS interception and no root certificates. AdVault only sees DNS queries.
Activity logs and statistics are stored on this device and can be cleared at any time.
Blocklists and provider data are downloaded over HTTPS and validated before use; downloaded content is never executed.
DNS filtering cannot block ads served from the same domain as the content (e.g. some video platforms).
Apps using their own DNS-over-HTTPS / DNS-over-TLS, or Android Private DNS, can bypass filtering.
Only one VPN can be active; AdVault cannot run alongside another VPN app.
Rewarded ads cannot be faked. Blocking them usually makes their rewards unavailable.
Aggressive mode may break features in some apps; use per-app Balanced mode or exclusions if needed.
“Estimated data saved” is an estimate, not a measurement.
